props.title: Under the Sun of Satan

sections.content: Maurice Pialat's Under the Sun of Satan (1987) marks a pivotal moment in French spiritual cinema, winning the Palme d'Or amid controversial booing at Cannes. Gérard Depardieu delivers a haunting performance as Donissan, a tormented priest wrestling with faith and evil in rural France. The film's stark approach to religious doubt connects directly to Robert Bresson's Diary of a Country Priest (1951), though Pialat rejects Bresson's austere style for a more visceral, emotionally raw treatment. Its unflinching examination of spiritual crisis influenced later works like Bruno Dumont's Hadewijch (2009) and Outside Satan (2011).

sections.content: The film's controversial portrayal of religious doubt connects to a broader tradition of French cinema questioning faith and institutional religion. Like Jean-Pierre Melville's Léon Morin, Priest (1961) and Alain Cavalier's Thérèse (1986), Pialat explores the intersection of carnal and spiritual existence. The raw confrontations between Donissan and Mouchette echo through later films like Xavier Beauvois's Of Gods and Men (2010), where religious conviction meets brutal reality.

Pialat's direction stands apart through its rejection of traditional religious film aesthetics. Unlike the transcendental style of Into Great Silence (2005) or the symbolic approach of The Passion of Joan of Arc (1928), Under the Sun of Satan employs harsh naturalism to explore supernatural themes. This influenced contemporary directors like Bruno Dumont and Cristian Mungiu's approach to religious subjects, particularly in Beyond the Hills (2012). SUBHEAD: Crisis of Faith in Modern Cinema

sections.content: The film's legacy is particularly evident in how it shaped depictions of clerical doubt in contemporary cinema. Paul Schrader's First Reformed (2017) and John Michael McDonagh's Calvary (2014) follow similar paths in examining priests confronting evil and despair in modern settings. These films share Pialat's interest in the physical manifestation of spiritual crisis, though they approach it through distinctly different cultural lenses.
